Who we are
A school built around every learner.
Discover the history, purpose and people behind an inclusive education centre committed to every learner’s growth.
Meet our teachers
Home About UsOur FoundationGrowing with our learners since 2017
Creative All Stars Academy began as a preschool in 2017 with 14 learners, three teachers and one driver. In 2020, the school introduced Grade 1 and began its expansion into primary education.
The school expanded again in 2023 with the introduction of upper primary classes. Our first KPSEA candidates sat the assessment in 2025, and Junior School opened in 2026.

Learning at CASA
Knowledge becomes something learners can use.
Our competency-based education approach develops practical skills, confident communication, values and meaningful progress.
Explore our classes
Home AcademicsCompetency-Based EducationLearning that develops the whole learner
Creative All Stars Academy follows Kenya's competency-based education approach. Teaching and learning focus on helping learners build knowledge, skills, values and attitudes that they can apply in school and everyday life.
The curriculum is delivered through age-appropriate, learner-centred experiences. Parents can contact the school for the current curriculum designs and the learning areas offered at a particular grade.
LEARNINGCore Learning Areas
The school supports balanced academic, practical, creative and values-based development. Exact learning areas vary by level and current curriculum design.
Mathematics
Learners develop numerical understanding, logical thinking and practical problem-solving skills.
English and Kiswahili
Language learning builds listening, speaking, reading and writing confidence.
Science and Technology
Learners explore their environment, investigate ideas and apply scientific and technological thinking.
Social Studies
Learning supports an understanding of community, citizenship, culture and the wider world.
Religious Education
Age-appropriate learning supports values, character development and respect for others.
Creative Arts
Creative experiences encourage imagination, expression, collaboration and appreciation of the arts.
SCHOOL SECTIONSLearning Pathway
A continuous journey from the early years through primary and into Junior School.
Stage 1
Early Years
Playgroup, PP1 and PP2 provide supportive, play-based foundations for language, numeracy, creativity, social development and independence.
Stage 2
Primary School
Grades 1 to 6 build knowledge, skills and values through learner-centred classroom experiences and practical application.
Stage 3
Junior School
The school introduced Grade 7 in 2026, extending its competency-based learning pathway into Junior School.
Assessment and Progress
Supporting progress throughout the learning journey
Teachers use ongoing classroom observation, learner tasks, projects and other age-appropriate assessment methods to understand progress and guide the next steps in learning. The school presented its first KPSEA candidates in 2025.

How the CBC Curriculum Prepares Learners for Real-World Problem Solving
Discover how Kenya’s Competency-Based Curriculum shifts the educational focus from rote memorization to skill mastery and creative solutions.
Creative All Stars Academy
Endeavour to Succeed
By Enock Maina · CASA Team 2025-05-10 5 min read
Back to blog directory
Home Blog How the CBC Curriculum Prepares Learners for Real-World Problem Solving
The transition from the traditional 8-4-4 education system to the Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC) marks one of the most progressive educational shifts in Kenyan history. For parents and teachers at Creative All Stars Academy, located in the heart of Nakuru, this shift is more than just a structural change—it is a cultural revolution in how children learn, think, and interact with the world.
The Heart of CBC: Skill Over Memorization
Under the old curriculum, students were largely assessed based on their ability to memorize formulas, dates, and spelling lists. CBC flips this script. It focuses on seven core competencies:
Communication and Collaboration
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving
Imagination and Creativity
Citizenship and Patriotism
Learning to Learn
Self-efficacy
Digital Literacy
Practical Application in Action
Take, for instance, a recent Grade 4 Agriculture project at our campus. Instead of reading about plant lifecycle solely from textbooks, students planted seedlings in recycled plastic containers, monitored daily growth, calculated water metrics, and discussed ecological impact. They applied mathematics, environmental conservation, and manual craftsmanship in a single project. This hands-on, multi-disciplinary approach ensures that knowledge is not merely stored, but lived.
Preparing for the Future
The modern global economy values adaptable individuals who can think on their feet, code, collaborate, and design. At Creative All Stars Academy, we embrace the CBC with open arms, integrating high-tech tools like computer labs and creative activities like dramatic elocution. We are not just training children to pass exams; we are nurturing the future leaders, innovators, and thinkers of Nakuru and the world.

Beyond the classroom
Talent grows when children get to try.
Our co-curricular programme creates space for wellbeing, creativity, teamwork, leadership and confident expression.
View school life
Home Co-CurricularWhole-Learner DevelopmentCo-Curricular Activities
Learners can explore a range of guided activities alongside their classroom learning.
01 Guidance and Counselling
Age-appropriate guidance that supports learners’ wellbeing, responsible choices and personal development.
02 Swimming
Swimming activities help learners develop confidence, coordination, fitness and water awareness.
03 Journalism
Learners practise observation, interviewing, writing and clear communication through school stories.
04 Games and Sports
Team games and physical activities build fitness, discipline, cooperation and sportsmanship.
05 Drama and Music
Performance activities give learners opportunities to develop creativity, expression and stage confidence.
06 Debate
Debate strengthens research, listening, public speaking and respectful presentation of ideas.
07 Scouting
Scouting develops practical life skills, service, teamwork, responsibility and leadership.
08 Health Club
The Health Club promotes hygiene, healthy choices and learner-led wellbeing awareness.
09 Modelling and Dance Club
Learners build confidence, rhythm, coordination and creative expression through modelling and dance.
